column1: # OVMX rd citation ledger -- DERIVED ARTIFACT. Do NOT hand-edit.
# Every gate that sells an exemption for a cited rd item id checks that id
# against this file. rd is nostr-backed and unreachable from CI, so the
# resolution happens on a host that has rd and the answer is committed.
# scanned:      src/, tools/ -- lines carrying an OVMX-<TOKEN>: marker
# open means:   the id appears in `rd list` (rd's own open set), not a
#               status name matched against a list kept in a gate.

column4: $QIO to a terminal never touches the executive device table: the public $ASSIGN/$QIO path byp...
Event flags are a per-process facade: sys_event.c never calls the executive and sys$ascefc fa...
The unwired families have LIVE per-process userspace impostors: the census declares the wrapp...
VMS process names are unobservable: no executive-resident process table, so prcnam dies at ex...
SET TERMINAL has no observable effect: it writes ctx->terminal, never IO$_SETMODE
Logical name tables are per-process fakes and VMSLNMD.EXE has zero clients
vms_kif_close and vms_kif_getlki have no product path and no owning item (no sys$getlki exists)
ASTs are delivered by the executive, not per-process
Rewire $ENQ/$DEQ to the kernel lock manager (single authoritative lock manager)
Executive owns the device table — SHOW DEVICE reflects real VMS devices
SHOW DEVICE / SHOW TERMINAL read the executive device table; VMS_TERMINAL env handoff deleted
Privileges and access modes are enforced by the executive
